name: B2recomp v0.2.10
body:
B2recomp v0.2.10 makes updating simple: from now on you unzip a new version over your old B2recomp folder, and the launcher rebuilds only what changed. Your saves, settings and mods stay. The game itself plays exactly as in v0.2.9. As always, this download contains no game files: the game is built on your PC from your own dump.

> **Opening an issue on GitHub:** it must be written **in English** and have **`b2recomp-report.zip` attached** (press **Report...** in the launcher). An issue opened without both will be closed promptly.

## New

- **Update by unzipping over your old folder.** When `B2recomp.exe` starts after an update, it shows the build screen with your dump folder already filled in and "B2recomp was updated: press Build". Build redoes only what changed (about a minute or two), then the launcher opens with your settings as you left them.
- **Your settings are never overwritten.** The download now brings its default settings in `config\defaults`; they are used only when your own `config\graphics.ini` or `config\controllers.ini` is missing.
- This works when updating from v0.2.9 or older, too.

## How to update from v0.2.x

1. Close B2recomp.
2. Unzip `B2recomp-builder-3558192.zip` to the same place as your old version, so that its `B2recomp` folder goes over your old `B2recomp` folder. When Windows asks, choose to replace the files.
3. Start `B2recomp.exe`, press **Build**, then **Play**.

## New install

1. Unzip `B2recomp-builder-3558192.zip` into a new folder.
2. Start `B2recomp.exe`, choose your dump folder and press **Build** (about 5 minutes on a 16-thread PC).
3. When the build is done, choose your settings and press **Play**.

Windows SmartScreen may warn about `B2recomp.exe` because it is not signed: choose "More info", then "Run anyway".

## Status

Tested on Windows: a v0.2.9 install updated to v0.2.10 by unzipping over it rebuilt in 1 min 13 s, with its settings, saves and mods unchanged. The game code is the same as in v0.2.9.

## Reporting a problem

Press **Report...** in the launcher. It makes `b2recomp-report.zip` in the B2recomp folder with the logs and your PC's details (Windows version, CPU, graphics card and driver), nothing of the game. Never attach game files.

**Issues must be written in English and must have `b2recomp-report.zip` attached. An issue opened without both will be closed promptly.**

SHA-256 of the zip: `441080bac5faf288946f1be59aa97e520152a3398c40379785d85887b272192f`

name: B2recomp v0.2.9
body:
B2recomp v0.2.9 makes **Frame rate (beta)** above 60 steadier: a freeze of the game world after some slow-motion moments is fixed, hit-stop, Witch Time and input windows keep their 60 fps timing, the pictures go out on a steady beat, and the renderer does less work every frame. At 60 fps (the default) the game plays as before. As always, this download contains no game files: the game is built on your PC from your own dump.

> **Opening an issue on GitHub:** it must be written **in English** and have **`b2recomp-report.zip` attached** (press **Report...** in the launcher). An issue opened without both will be closed promptly.

## Fixed (Frame rate above 60)

- **The world no longer freezes after a slow motion.** At the end of some slow-motion moments in events, the game could stand still for 5 to 30 seconds at 120 fps, with the music still playing, until a longer frame came by. Fixed, and slow motions now last as long as at 60 fps.
- **Hit-stop, Witch Time and input windows keep their timing.** Some of the game's timers only count for a while after an event: the pause when a hit lands, the end of Witch Time, input windows, enemy holds and waits. Above 60 fps they ran twice as fast; they now count in 60 fps frames (79 more of them, 114 in all).
- **Steadier pictures.** Above 60 fps each picture went out the moment it was ready, so small differences in the work of each frame reached the screen. Pictures now go out on a steady beat, as at 60: on a 240 Hz (or 238 Hz) monitor the frames are shown for two refreshes each. In our tests the frames shown unevenly went from about 13 % to under 3 %, and to 0.36 % in a 17-minute played session.

## Faster

- **Less work for the renderer every frame.** Vertex data that does not change stays on the graphics card instead of being copied again every frame (in fights 17 to 36 MB a frame were copied, almost all of it unchanged); the check for which textures the game has changed asks Windows once per group of textures instead of once per texture; the log's reports are written at once. In our test fight at 120 fps the renderer now needs about 3.2 ms a frame instead of about 5 ms, and late frames are rarer. At 60 fps the same savings apply.

## How to use

1.  Unzip `B2recomp-builder-5e03296.zip` into a new folder.
2. Start `B2recomp.exe`, choose your dump folder and press **Build** (about 5 minutes on a 16-thread PC)
3. When the build is done, choose your settings and press **Play**.

**Updating from v0.2.x:** after the build, copy these folders from your old B2recomp folder into the new one:
- `build\play\userdata` (your saves);
- `config` (your settings and controls);
- optionally `cache`, so the game does not prepare its shaders again on the first start.

Windows SmartScreen may warn about `B2recomp.exe` because it is not signed: choose "More info", then "Run anyway".

## Status 

Tested on Windows with an NVIDIA card and a 238 Hz monitor: played at 120 fps (fights, and the spot where the world froze), and checked with our test route at 60 and at 120 fps, with every check passing and no slowdown at either. Frame rates above 60 are still a beta.

## Reporting a problem

Press **Report...** in the launcher. It makes `b2recomp-report.zip` in the B2recomp folder with the logs and your PC's details (Windows version, CPU, graphics card and driver), nothing of the game. Never attach game files.

**Issues must be written in English and must have `b2recomp-report.zip` attached. An issue opened without both will be closed promptly.**

SHA-256 of the zip: `bf8ac95df3fceb1912c18fe69a643c713eafc7f32a66ff0fe0300ca705badc0c`

name: Linux Test 7
body:
This is the seventh **test release of the native Linux version** of B2recomp. It is a pre-release: the Windows version is **v0.2.9**. As always, this download contains no game files: the game is built on your PC from your own dump.

> **Opening an issue on GitHub:** it must be written **in English** and have **the report attached** (`b2recomp-report.tar.gz`: press **Report...** in the launcher, or run `sh scripts/report.sh`). An issue opened without both will be closed promptly.

## New since Linux Test 6

The fixes of Windows v0.2.9. Most matter only with **Frame rate (beta)** above 60; at 60 fps the game plays as before.

- **The world no longer freezes after a slow motion.** At the end of some slow-motion moments in events, the game could stand still for 5 to 30 seconds at 120 fps, with the music still playing, until a longer frame came by. Fixed, and slow motions now last as long as at 60 fps.
- **Hit-stop, Witch Time and input windows keep their timing.** Some of the game's timers only count for a while after an event: the pause when a hit lands, the end of Witch Time, input windows, enemy holds and waits. Above 60 fps they ran twice as fast; they now count in 60 fps frames (79 more of them, 114 in all).
- **Steadier pictures above 60 fps.** Pictures go out on a steady beat at the chosen frame rate instead of the moment each one is ready. On Linux the beat is the game's own clock (the Linux version has no display lock yet).
- **The log's reports are written at once** instead of in dozens of small writes (a late frame every 300 frames at 120 fps).
- Two of v0.2.9's speed-ups depend on Windows tracking which memory the game wrote (vertex data kept on the graphics card, the texture check in groups). The Linux version has no such tracking yet, so they change nothing on Linux.

## Updating from an earlier Linux test release

Unzip `B2recomp-linux-builder-affeda0.zip` over your old B2recomp folder and start `B2recomp`. It says that B2recomp was updated; press **Build** (a short rebuild, about two minutes), then **Play**. Your settings and saves stay.

## New install

1. Unzip `B2recomp-linux-builder-affeda0.zip` where you want to keep the game, for example `~/Games`.
2. Open the folder and start `B2recomp`: double-click it, or in a terminal run `sh ./B2recomp`.
3. Choose your dump folder (one folder that holds `exefs/` and `romfs/` of Bayonetta 2, version 1.2), press **Build** (5 to 20 minutes, depending on your CPU), then **Play**.

You need 64-bit Linux from about 2022 or newer with a desktop (X11 or Wayland) and a Vulkan 1.3 driver (Mesa for AMD and Intel, or NVIDIA's own driver). `START HERE.txt` in the zip has the details.

## Known limits of this test release

- The game times its frames with its own clock, not with your monitor's refresh as the Windows version does. You may see a slight judder now and then.
- The renderer finds out which textures the game changed by checksumming them (on Windows the system tracks this), which costs a little more CPU per frame.
- The v0.2.9 fixes were tested on Windows; the Linux build compiles the same changes, but they have not been tried on Linux yet.
- Tested on Arch-based systems (CachyOS) with an NVIDIA RTX 4060 laptop and an AMD RX 560, on KDE and Hyprland (Wayland). Other distributions should work, but are untested.

## Reporting problems

Press **Report...** in the launcher, or run `sh scripts/report.sh` in the B2recomp folder. It makes `b2recomp-report.tar.gz` with the logs and your PC's details, and nothing of the game. Never attach game files.

**Issues must be written in English and must have the report attached. An issue opened without both will be closed promptly.**

SHA-256 of the zip: `aad8409b14c2f9d5735e49f1848ce0942f839e5348e99a801e88751606da2d30`

name: B2recomp v0.2.7
body:
B2recomp v0.2.7 fixes a blurry picture on screens with display scaling and a crash in Tag Climax’s online mode. As before, this download contains no game files: the game is built on your PC from your own dump.

## Disclaimer 

If you decide to open a issue, give me a couple details about your situation in the best wording you can put it in ( English Only) then supply the report zip. If both of these things are not done when opening the issue it will be closed accordingly ( Can't do anything blind )

## Next Update will include better stability hopefully across all systems, working on adding HDR support after this next release. So for now have HDR DISABLED when playing the Recomp or your game will break if you open a issue about it when I'm already telling you to turn it off for now It will be closed promptly.

## Fixed

- Sharp picture on screens with display scaling. On a screen where Windows display scaling is above 100 % (common on 4K monitors and laptops), Windows gave the game a smaller “virtual” screen and stretched its picture: on a 4K screen at 300 %, the game drew 1280 × 720 and Windows enlarged it three times, so even a high Resolution scale looked blurry. The game now tells Windows it handles scaling itself: Borderless and Fullscreen use your screen’s real resolution, and a Windowed game keeps the size it had before. At 100 % scaling nothing changes.
- Tag Climax online no longer closes the game. Choosing Online and then Quick Match showed “Error Code: 2618-0006” and then the game closed. Online play cannot work in B2recomp (it cannot connect to Nintendo’s online services), but now the game says so properly: a short message explains that online play is not available, the game shows its own “Not connected to the Internet.” and you are back in the Online Menu.


## How to use

1. Unzip B2recomp-builder-b3a6dc6.zip into a new folder.
2. Start B2recomp.exe, choose your dump folder and press Build (about 5 minutes on a 16-thread PC).
3. When the build is done, choose your settings and press Play.

Updating from v0.2.x: after the build, copy these folders from your old B2recomp folder into the new one:

- build\play\userdata (your saves);
- config (your settings and controls);
- optionally cache, so the game does not prepare its shaders again on the first start.

Windows SmartScreen may warn about B2recomp.exe because it is not signed: choose “More info”, then “Run anyway”.

## Status 

Both fixes were tested on Windows with an NVIDIA card: the display scaling fix at 100 % scaling and with a switch to 150 % while playing borderless (the window sizes for scaled screens were checked with a test setting), the Tag Climax fix by choosing Quick Match several times. If something looks wrong, a report helps: press Report... in the launcher and attach b2recomp-report.zip to an issue (never attach game files).

name: B2recomp v0.2.6
body:
B2recomp v0.2.6 fixes missing icons and colours on AMD Radeon cards and makes crash reports more useful. As before, this download contains no game files: the game is built on your PC from your own dump.

## DISCLAIMER 

- If you decide to open a issue, give me a couple details about your situation in the best wording you can put it in then supply the report zip. If both of these things are not done when opening the issue it will be closed accordingly ( Can't do anything blind ) Also make sure your AMD drivers are up to date and that you have the latest release of the recomp.

## Fixed 

- Missing icons and colours on AMD Radeon cards (seen on an RX 6950 XT). Some of the game’s textures came out blank: the tutorial’s combo icons, the letters on the button icons, and the colour of the health bars. When B2recomp creates a texture, it first clears it and then copies the game’s pixels in. Nothing told the graphics driver to keep that order: NVIDIA’s driver kept it anyway, while AMD’s sometimes ran the clear last, wiping the picture. The two steps are now explicitly ordered. On NVIDIA cards nothing changes on screen, and the speed is the same.

## Better reports 

- How the game ended. If the game closes unexpectedly, the launcher now writes the exit code and what it means as the last line of the game’s log (build\play\stdout.txt).
- Windows’ own crash records. The Report... zip now includes windows-errors.txt: the crash (Application Error) and hang (Application Hang) records Windows kept of B2recomp’s programs over the last 30 days. They show crashes that the game’s own error handling never sees, for example a crash inside the graphics driver.
- The exact build. The builder package now has a VERSION file, so a report names the build it came from.

## How to use

1. Unzip B2recomp-builder-60f5552.zip into a new folder.
2. Start B2recomp.exe, choose your dump folder and press Build (about 5 minutes on a 16-thread PC).
3. When the build is done, choose your settings and press Play.

## Updating from v0.2.x: after the build, copy these folders from your old B2recomp folder into the new one:

- build\play\userdata (your saves);
- config (your settings and controls);
- optionally cache, so the game does not prepare its shaders again on the first start.

Windows SmartScreen may warn about B2recomp.exe because it is not signed: choose “More info”, then “Run anyway”.

## Status

The texture fix was tested on an NVIDIA card: the blank textures were reproduced there on purpose, the fixed build plays the standard test route with no errors, and its speed is unchanged. It has not been confirmed on an AMD card yet. If you have one, a report after the tutorial helps: press Report... in the launcher and attach b2recomp-report.zip to an issue (never attach game files).

SHA-256 of the zip: c5255bf7ac3bd9c9eb970dc88e97f03b9cf856d2447cebf96150d75ce856b281

The game plays its cinematics at 30 frames per second and holds the last picture of every shot for one of its frames before it cuts to the next shot. At 120 fps that hold was four times too short, so every cut gained a little time. The hold now lasts as long as the game intended at any frame rate. At 60 fps nothing changes. If you set the frame rate to 60 only for the cinematics, you can set it back to 120.

**Updating from v0.2.x:** after the build, copy these folders from your old B2recomp folder into the new one:

- `build\play\userdata` (your saves);
- `config` (your settings and controls);
- optionally `cache`, so the game does not prepare its shaders again on the first start.

The fix is applied while the game is built, so a new **Build** is needed: copying files into an old folder is not enough.

Windows SmartScreen may warn about `B2recomp.exe` because it is not signed: choose "More info", then "Run anyway".

## Status 

Tested on an NVIDIA card at 120 fps with the prologue cinematic, compared with 60 fps picture by picture and against the sound, and in the first fight (no change there). name: B2recomp v0.2.4: AMD effects fix, cinematic sound sync on G-Sync / FreeSync screens
body:
B2recomp v0.2.4 fixes two problems players reported: effects missing on AMD Radeon cards, and sound drifting away from the pictures on G-Sync / FreeSync screens. As before, this download contains no game files: the game is built on your PC from your own dump.

### DISCLAIMER 
If you decide to open a issue, give me a couple details about your situation in the best wording you can put it in then supply the report zip. If both of these things are not done when opening the issue it will be closed accordingly ( Can't do anything blind ) Also make sure your AMD drivers are up to date and that you have the latest release of the recomp.

## Fixed 

1. Missing effects on AMD Radeon cards (seen on an RX 9070). AMD’s driver refused a few particle shaders, so some effects were not drawn (the log showed THE DRIVER REFUSED lines). Those shaders read a buffer that B2recomp never connected to them: NVIDIA’s driver lets that pass, AMD’s refuses the shader. They are now correct. On the first start only these few shaders are prepared again; everything else in your shader cache stays as it is.
2. Sound out of sync in the cinematics on variable-refresh screens (G-Sync / FreeSync). With Vertical sync on Auto, the game’s speed follows the screen’s refresh. A variable-refresh screen can run a little slower than its nominal rate, and the game then ran up to about 2 % slower than the sound, so voices and lips drifted apart. Auto now checks the game’s speed every few seconds: when the refresh drifts, the program’s own 60 Hz clock takes over, and when the refresh is steady again the game follows the screen again. On a screen with a steady 60, 120 or 240 Hz nothing changes. Display still follows the screen in every case, as you chose. If you set Vertical sync to Program clock as a workaround, you can set it back to Auto.


## How To Use

1. Unzip B2recomp-builder-6dfe53c.zip into a new folder.
2. Start B2recomp.exe, choose your dump folder and press Build (about 5 minutes on a 16-thread PC).
3. When the build is done, choose your settings and press Play.

Updating from v0.2.x: after the build, copy these folders from your old B2recomp folder into the new one:

- build\play\userdata (your saves);
- config (your settings and controls);
- optionally cache, so the game does not prepare its shaders again on the first start.

Windows SmartScreen may warn about B2recomp.exe because it is not signed: choose “More info”, then “Run anyway”.

## Status

Both fixes were tested on an NVIDIA card; they are not yet confirmed on an AMD card or a variable-refresh screen. If you have one, a report after a few minutes of play helps: press Report... in the launcher and attach b2recomp-report.zip to an issue (never attach game files).

SHA-256 of the zip: 4b57262c7fe242052cb33fd5a1d259ee44c6dde25e48b4dfe2ce964c948cb7b4

name: B2recomp Linux Test 2
body:
This is the second test release of the native Linux version of B2recomp. It is a pre-release: the Windows version is v0.2.4. As always, this download contains no game files: the game is built on your PC from your own dump.

### NEW SINCE LINUX TEST 1
The fixes of Windows v0.2.4

- Particle shaders corrected for every graphics driver. A few particle shaders read a buffer that B2recomp never connected to them. NVIDIA’s drivers let that pass, while AMD’s Windows driver refused those shaders, so some effects were missing there. They are now correct on every driver, including Mesa on Linux. On the first start only these few shaders are prepared again.

- Vertical sync = Auto on G-Sync / FreeSync screens. This fixes the sound drifting away from the pictures in the cinematics on Windows. On Linux it changes nothing yet: the Linux version still times its frames with its own 60 Hz clock (see “Known limits”), which never had this drift.


## Updating from Linux Test 1

Unzip B2recomp-linux-builder-a695915.zip over your old B2recomp folder and start B2recomp. It says that B2recomp was updated; press Build (a short rebuild, about two minutes), then Play. Your settings and saves stay.

## New Install 

1. Unzip B2recomp-linux-builder-a695915.zip where you want to keep the game, for example ~/Games.
2. Open the folder and start B2recomp: double-click it, or in a terminal run sh ./B2recomp.
3. Choose your dump folder (one folder that holds exefs/ and romfs/ of Bayonetta 2, version 1.2), press Build (5 to 20 minutes, depending on your CPU), then Play.

You need 64-bit Linux from about 2022 or newer with a desktop (X11 or Wayland) and a Vulkan 1.3 driver (Mesa for AMD and Intel, or NVIDIA’s own driver). START HERE.txt in the zip has the details.

## Known limits of this test release 

- The game times its frames with its own 60 Hz clock, not with your monitor’s refresh as the Windows version does. On a screen that is not exactly 60 Hz you may see a slight judder now and then.
- The renderer finds out which textures the game changed by checksumming them (on Windows the system tracks this), which costs a little more CPU per frame.
- Tested on Arch-based systems (CachyOS) with an NVIDIA RTX 4060 laptop and an AMD RX 560, on KDE and Hyprland (Wayland). Other distributions should work, but are untested.

## Reporting problems

Press Report... in the launcher, or run sh scripts/report.sh in the B2recomp folder. It makes b2recomp-report.tar.gz with the logs and your PC’s details, and nothing of the game. Attach it to an issue with a few words on what happened. Never attach game files.

name: B2Recomp v0.2.2 Smoother frame timing after stalls on certain System Setups
body:
B2recomp v0.2.2 is a small fix for smoother motion on some PCs. As before, this download contains no game files: the game is built on your PC from your own dump.

### DISCLAIMER - If you open a issue with no stdout.txt It will be closed accordingly I can't go into your issue and help resolve it being blind to what is going on to the game on your system compared to what your telling me.

##  Side Note: Nvidia cards have had no reported issue so far which is what this was originally developed for so AMD cards are bound to encounter issues on windows bc the Vulkan 1.3 driver lacks features on Windows But not Linux so they may be the alternative for AMD for now once I release the linux version 



##Fixed 

- **Uneven motion after a short stall.** The game times its frames to your monitor's refresh. On a slower PC (reported on an RX 560 with an i7-4770), a stall of a tenth of a second during play switched that off for the rest of the session, so one frame was shown twice about every 5 seconds. Now the game locks to the refresh again a second later. Nothing changes on PCs where this never happened.
- Included from v0.2.1: the start-up crash with error code 6 on an RX 9070 XT, and tearing / flickering on AMD cards.

## How to use

1. Unzip `B2recomp-builder-870d9ab.zip` into a new folder.
2. Start `B2recomp.exe`, choose your dump folder and press **Build** (about 5 minutes on a 16-thread PC).
3. When the build is done, choose your settings and press **Play**.

**Updating from v0.2.0 or v0.2.1:** copy the `build\play\userdata` folder (your saves) and the `config` folder (your settings and controls) from your old B2recomp folder into the new one after the build. You can also copy the `cache` folder, so the game does not prepare its shaders again on the first start.

Windows SmartScreen may warn about `B2recomp.exe` because it is not signed: choose "More info", then "Run anyway".

## Status 

Tested on one Windows 11 PC with an NVIDIA GPU (the stall was simulated there). Logs from players (`build\play\stdout.txt`) are very welcome, especially from AMD cards. Please report problems on the Issues page (never attach game files).

name: B2 Recomp v0.2.1: AMD fixes
body:
## Fixed

- **The game stopped at start with error code 6 on an AMD Radeon RX 9070 XT** (`vkCreateGraphicsPipelines ... VK_ERROR_INITIALIZATION_FAILED` in the log). The graphics driver refused to prepare one of the game's shaders, and the game treated that as fatal. Now that shader is prepared another way; if the driver refuses that too, only what is drawn with it is left out, and the game goes on. The log then has a `THE DRIVER REFUSED` line: please report it, with your GPU and driver version, so the shader can be fixed properly.
-  **Flickering (tearing) on AMD cards**, reported on an RX 560. AMD's Windows driver lacks the presentation mode the game used for smooth, tear-free frames, so the picture tore through the middle of the screen. The game now uses the driver's vertical sync instead whenever that mode is missing. **Vertical sync** in the launcher works as before; **Off** still allows tearing for the lowest latency. Nothing changes on NVIDIA cards.
- ** Side note Nvidia cards have had no reported issue so far which is what this was originally developed for so AMD cards are bound to encounter issues and bugs.


## How to use

1. Unzip `B2recomp-builder-781e756.zip` into a new folder.
2. Start `B2recomp.exe`, choose your dump folder and press **Build** (about 5 minutes on a 16-thread PC).
3. When the build is done, choose your settings and press **Play**.


**Updating from v0.2.0:** copy the `build\play\userdata` folder (your saves) and the `config` folder (your settings and controls) from your old B2recomp folder into the new one after the build.

## Status

- Tested on one Windows 11 PC with an NVIDIA GPU; the AMD fixes were checked there by simulating the AMD driver's behaviour, and are not yet confirmed on the AMD cards themselves. Logs from AMD players (`build\play\stdout.txt`) are very welcome. Please report problems on the Issues page (never attach game files).

name: B2recomp v0.2.0
body:
New

- Keyboard and mouse. A layout like the original Bayonetta on PC: W A S D to move, the mouse for the camera, left / right mouse to punch and kick, Space to jump, left Shift to dodge, left Alt to lock on, Q for Umbran Climax, Esc to pause. They work alongside a controller. Keyboard and mouse... in the launcher rebinds any action (two keys or mouse buttons each) and sets the mouse sensitivity. Input can lock the game to the keyboard and mouse only, or to the controller only.
- Mods, as on the Switch emulators. Put mods for the Switch version into a mods\ folder beside B2recomp.exe and switch them on or off with Mods... in the launcher. Texture, model and sound mods (romfs\) work at the next start. Code mods (.pchtxt, .ips) are built into the game: Apply (rebuild) takes about a minute, with the game closed.
- PlayStation or Xbox button pictures. Choose them under Button prompts after adding Timo654’s Controller Prompts Replacement (DS4/XBOX) (GameBanana 360121, Switch version) to mods\. On Auto, the game shows the buttons of the controller you play with.
- Frame rate (beta): 60 to 120 fps. A launcher slider. Above 60 the game shows more frames per second at its normal speed: its clock follows the real frame time and its main timers are converted. This is experimental: some effects, menus and button-mash prompts may still run faster, and cinematics run at the chosen rate. 60 is the default and the game exactly as made.
- A step-by-step guide for new players in the README.

Fixed 

- Character shadows were missing or collapsed (most visible when looking down), and the automatic exposure did not adapt. The game reads some of its rendered images back on the CPU to place its shadows and to measure brightness; those images now reach it, without the game waiting for the graphics card.
- Included from v0.1.1 and v0.1.2: games without the system fonts no longer stop at start, and AMD Radeon RX 400 / 500 cards use a fallback path.


How to use 

1. Unzip B2recomp-builder-247617b.zip into a new folder.
2. Start B2recomp.exe, choose your dump folder and press Build (about 5 minutes on a 16-thread PC).
3. When the build is done, choose your settings and press Play.
Optional: This is a question for people on Linux, will you try and load this through steam/proton or wine and make a issue on the repo  so I can know if this works or not  


Updating from v0.1.x: to keep your saves, copy the build\play\userdata folder from your old B2recomp folder into the new one after the build. You can copy the old folder’s config\graphics.ini over too; set the controls again in the launcher (an old controllers.ini would keep the old keyboard keys).

Windows SmartScreen may warn about B2recomp.exe because it is not signed: choose “More info”, then “Run anyway”.


Status 

- Tested on one Windows 11 PC with an NVIDIA GPU. Later chapters, AMD and Intel GPUs and Windows 10 are not fully tested yet. Expect bugs; please report them on the Issues page (never attach game files).

body:
AMD Radeon RX 400 / 500 (Polaris)
These cards run the full renderer on Linux. On Windows, AMD’s driver for them lacks Vulkan features B2recomp normally uses (dynamic vertex input, pipeline libraries, mailbox vsync), so the Windows version takes a slower path there, with more shader building while you play. Their speed in fights is often set by the processor these PCs have: a 4-core CPU from around 2013 gives a steady 30 fps there, while menus and cutscenes stay at 60.

Tested on Arch-based systems (CachyOS) with an NVIDIA RTX 4060 laptop and an AMD RX 560, on KDE and Hyprland (Wayland). Other distributions should work, but are untested.
Reporting problems
Press Report... in the launcher, or run sh scripts/report.sh in the B2recomp folder. It makes b2recomp-report.tar.gz with the logs and your PC’s details, and nothing of the game. Attach it to an issue with a few words on what happened. Never attach game files.

name: B2recomp v0.1.2: font and RX 400/500 fixes
body:
Bug-fix release for two start-up problems players reported. Same use as before; this download still contains no game files.

## Fixed

- **The game stopped right after the first frame when the dump had no system fonts** (`shared font 0 NOT FOUND ... stopping` in the log). The fonts are now optional, as the documentation said: without them a font of your PC (Yu Gothic, Meiryo, Segoe UI or Arial) stands in. If you do have your console's shared fonts, put them in `<dump>\sysdata\fonts\` before building, or in `B2recomp\targets\sysdata\fonts\` later, as `.ttf` or as the console's `.bfttf` files. See "System fonts" in BUILDING.md.
- **AMD Radeon RX 400 / RX 500 cards (RX 460-590) stopped at start** with `NOT IMPLEMENTED ... a GPU without VK_EXT_vertex_input_dynamic_state`. AMD's Windows driver does not offer that feature for these cards, so the game now uses a fallback path there. It is tested in a simulation only, not on a real RX 400/500 card yet: if you have one, please post your `build\play\stdout.txt`. On those cards the first runs may hitch a little more while the graphics are prepared.

Nothing changes for GPUs that already worked: their shader cache stays valid.

## How to use

1. Unzip `B2recomp-builder-1642dd6.zip` anywhere (a new folder, or replace your old one and build again).
2. Start `B2recomp.exe`, choose your dump folder and press **Build** (about 5 minutes on a 16-thread PC).
3. When the build is done, choose your settings and press **Play**.

Windows SmartScreen may warn about `B2recomp.exe` because it is not signed: choose "More info", then "Run anyway".

name: B2recomp 0.1.0 (first test release)
body:
First test release of B2recomp, an unofficial static recompilation of Bayonetta 2 (Nintendo Switch) for Windows.

This download contains no game files. It holds the B2recomp source code and the free tools needed to build it (compiler, Python, SDL3, Vulkan headers, shader-compiler shim, Microsoft Visual C++ runtime files), with their licences. The game itself is built on your PC from your own legally dumped copy.

What you need
Your own extracted copy of Bayonetta 2, version 1.2 (update v131072): a folder with exefs\ and romfs\ (see BUILDING.md)
Windows 10/11 x64 and a GPU with a Vulkan 1.3 driver
About 15 GB of disk space (your dump plus about 1.2 GB for this package and the build)
How to use
Unzip B2recomp-builder-330e59a.zip anywhere.
Start B2recomp.exe, choose your dump folder (Browse, or drag it onto the window) and press Build. It takes about 5 minutes on a 16-thread PC, longer on smaller ones.
When the build is done the window becomes the launcher: choose your settings and press Play. The first start prepares the game’s shaders once, which takes several minutes.
Windows SmartScreen may warn about B2recomp.exe because it is not signed: choose “More info”, then “Run anyway”.

Status
Tested on one Windows 11 PC: the prologue plays through and chapter 1 is playable with a controller. Later chapters, other GPUs (AMD, Intel) and Windows 10 are not tested yet. Expect bugs; please report them on the Issues page (never attach game files).
